newsitem.title: TURKEY: Albania seeks help from Black Sea countries.
newsitem.headline: Albania seeks help from Black Sea countries.

text.p: Albanian government officials attending a conference of Black Sea countries in Istanbul asked for help on Tuesday to restore their ailing economy.

"It is our most sincere hope that through the support of Black Sea Economic Cooperation (BSEC), our beautiful country will once again find the place it merits among European countries," Mirgjind Pefiku, director general of Albania's foreign relations department, told reporters.
Albania's economy faced collapse amid widespread unrest following the failure of get-rich-quick "pyramid" schemes earlier this year.
Thousands of Albanians took to the streets demanding the resignation of President Sali Berisha, and looting state arsenals. Unofficial estimates suggest more than 300 people died in the violence.
Armed rebels, who blame Berisha for the dubious investment schemes disaster, are still in control of much of southern Albania.

"The crisis cannot be passed without the help of the international community. Our economy cannot now provide compensation for losses during the emergency. It would be very useful if BSEC could...help save Albania," said Enika Abazi, an official from Albania's ministry of transport and trade.

BSEC, the brainchild of former Turkish President Turgut Ozal, was set up in 1992. Member countries include Turkey, Greece, Moldova, Albania, Bulgaria, Romania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Ukraine and Russia.

The group has a secretariat in Istanbul, a parliamentary assembly, a private-sector business council, an economic data centre and several working bodies. A Black Sea Trade and Development Bank will open in Thesalloniki in May.
But it has undertaken no projects so far, and conference organisers hope the Istanbul conference will come up with concrete plans.

Six heads of state, ministers of transport, economy and communication, representatives of the World Bank, the European Bank of Reconstruction and Development and the International Finance Corporation, and some 600 businessmen are attending the conference.
